title: 은/는과 이/가: 언제 무엇을 쓸까요?
objective: Learners can attach the right form of each particle after a final consonant or a vowel (책은/책이, 친구는/친구가). They can choose 이/가 for question words and their answers (누가 왔어요? — 민수가 왔어요) and with 있어요/없어요/아파요 (머리가 아파요), and choose 은/는 to introduce a topic or show contrast (저는 학생이에요; 고기는 먹어요, 생선은 안 먹어요). They can also fix three common form errors: *저가 → 제가, *나가 → 내가, *누구가 → 누가.
summary: Korean has two small words that often come right after a noun: the topic particle 은/는 and the subject particle 이/가. This sheet shows how to pick the right shape after a consonant or a vowel. It also shows when to use 이/가 (question words, answers, 있어요/없어요/아파요) and when to use 은/는 (topics and contrast). It also covers three short forms learners often get wrong: 제가, 내가 and 누가.

task.title: CHOOSE AND FIX PARTICLES
task.line: Fill in or choose the right particle, and rewrite each wrong sentence correctly.

forms.when: Use these when the noun ends in a consonant (받침), e.g. 책, 식당, 음식.
forms.means: 은 marks the topic (what you are talking about). 이 marks the subject (who or what does or is something).
forms.exampleMeaning: The food at this restaurant is tasty.

forms.when: Use these when the noun ends in a vowel, e.g. 친구, 키, 커피.
forms.means: These mean the same as 은 and 이. Only the shape changes.

forms.form: 이/가 with question words and their answers
forms.when: Use these with question words such as 누가, 뭐가 and 어디가, and with the noun that answers them.
forms.means: The question word and its answer are new information, so they take 이/가, not 은/는. Note: 누구 + 가 = 누가.
forms.example: 뭐가 제일 맛있어요? — 김치찌개가 제일 맛있어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: What's the tastiest? — The kimchi stew is the tastiest.

forms.when: Use these for the thing that exists or doesn't exist, or the body part that hurts.
forms.means: "There is / there isn't X" or "my X hurts"
forms.exampleMeaning: I have a stomachache. Do you have any medicine at home?

forms.when: Use it to say what the sentence is about, often yourself or something you are describing.
forms.means: "As for X…" It sets up the topic, and the rest of the sentence tells you about it.

forms.when: Use it when you compare two things, e.g. one is true and the other is not.
forms.means: "X is like this, (but) Y is like that."
forms.exampleMeaning: I'm busy today, but tomorrow is fine.

watchOut: 저가 (X) → 제가 (O): When 저 (I, polite) takes 가, it changes to 제가.
나가 (X) → 내가 (O): When 나 (I, casual) takes 가, it changes to 내가.
누구가 (X) → 누가 (O): When 누구 (who) takes 가, it shortens to 누가.
책가 (X) → 책이 (O): 책 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이, not 가.
exercises: Fill in each blank with 은 or 는: 지하철____ 빨라요. 버스____ 느려요.
Fill in each blank with 이 or 가: 어깨____ 아파요. 그런데 오늘은 시간____ 없어요.
Fill in the blanks. The first blank asks "who": ____ 전화했어요? — 수진____ 전화했어요.
Correct the mistake: 저가 창문을 닫을게요.
Correct the mistake in B's line: A: 누가 설거지할 거야? B: 나가 할게.
You are meeting someone for the first time. Choose the right words: 안녕하세요? (저는 / 제가) 마리아예요. 스페인 사람이에요.
